topics.title: Vol II: Fireground Support, Loss Control & Overhaul (202) (Part 1)
topics.sub: Fireground factors, Resource Sector, support activities, attack teams, loss control and salvage.
concepts: 202.02: Size-up sorts info into 7 Critical Fireground Factors (Building, Fire, Occupancy, Life Hazard, Arrangement, Resources, Other); gathered by visual, recon and preplan; keep revising the plan.
202.07: Resource Sector = equipment pool near the scene but outside the perimeter; high-rise: 5 floors below on-deck, radio name includes floor ("Resource 25").
202.09: Ventilate to prevent mushrooming and gain entry; interior sector decides vent; bowstring with attic fire = search then defensive; no roof on tile-roof SFR attic fires.
202.10: Standard Attack Team = 2 engines + 1 ladder (forward pumper fed by key pumper).
202.12 / 202.12A: Loss control in all 3 priorities (benchmark "Loss stopped"); attack from unburned side; salvage starts beside/below the fire; group, raise and cover contents.

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.02, the Critical Fireground Factors help the IC simplify complex size-up information into how many distinct categories?
cards.a: Seven distinct categories.
cards.why: M.P. 202.02: The factors simplify complex information "into 7 distinct categories" (Building, Fire, Occupancy, Life Hazard, Arrangement, Resources, Other).

cards.q: From the command post you can't see the rear of a strip mall, so you assign a company to do a 360 and report back. Per M.P. 202.02, which form of size-up is this?
cards.a: Reconnaissance.
cards.why: M.P. 202.02: Reconnaissance is information not visually available to Command from outside, gained by sending someone to "check-out, go-see", generally a 360-degree recon with a report back.

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.02, when Command starts an attack on an incomplete initial size-up, the remaining questions about structure, conditions or occupancy are called what?
cards.a: Critical unknown information.
cards.why: M.P. 202.02: Unanswered questions after an initial size-up are "defined as critical unknown information", and efforts must continue to improve that information.

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.02, "number of occupants" and "characteristics of escape routes" are listed under which fireground factor category?
cards.a: Life Hazard.
cards.why: M.P. 202.02: Life Hazard covers number, location and condition of occupants, search and rescue commitment, and avenues of escape.

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.02, built-in sprinklers/standpipes and the adequacy of water supply fall under which fireground factor category?
cards.a: Resources.
cards.why: M.P. 202.02: Resources includes hydrants, supplemental water, adequacy of water supply and "built-in private fire protection (sprinkler, standpipe, alarms)".

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.02, what's the right attitude toward the incident action plan you built in the first few minutes of a fire?
cards.a: Keep revising it as fireground factors change, based on information feedback.
cards.why: M.P. 202.02: "Beware of developing an incident action plan and sticking to that same plan throughout the fire"; effective operations require continual revisions.
opts: Revise it as fireground factors change
Stick with it, since changing plans midstream confuses crews
Revise it only at each 10-minute elapsed-time notice
Change it only after Command has been transferred

cards.q: At a high-rise fire, per M.P. 202.07 where is the Resource Sector normally established?
cards.a: Five floors below the on-deck floor (or another safe, uncontaminated area below the fire).
cards.why: M.P. 202.07: For high-rise operations Resource is "normally established five floors below the on-deck floor" or another safe, uncontaminated environment below the fire.
opts: Five floors below the on-deck floor
Two floors below the fire floor
In the lobby, next to Lobby Sector
Three floors below the on-deck floor

cards.q: Resource Sector at a high-rise fire is set up on the 25th floor. Per M.P. 202.07, what radio designation should it use?
cards.a: "Resource 25."
cards.why: M.P. 202.07: The radio designation "should include the floor number that Resource is located on (e.g., 'Resource 25')" so crews can find it.

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.07, where should a Resource Sector be set up at a typical (non-high-rise) incident?
cards.a: Close to operations, but outside the fireground/medical perimeter in a safe location.
cards.why: M.P. 202.07: Resource "should be established in close proximity to the scene of operations, but outside of the defined fireground/medical incident perimeter in a safe location."
opts: Near operations but outside the incident perimeter
Inside the perimeter, beside the sector it supports
At Level II Staging, alongside uncommitted apparatus
Next to the command post so Command tracks inventory

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.07, how should equipment in the Resource Sector pool be organized?
cards.a: Grouped by type, showing equipment that is ready for use and equipment that is depleted.
cards.why: M.P. 202.07: Resource maintains an inventory at all times, and equipment areas "should be grouped by type, denoting equipment that is ready for use and equipment that is depleted."
opts: By type, marking ready-for-use vs. depleted
By the company that brought it, for later return
In one central pile with an officer issuing items
By the operating sector expected to request it

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.07, besides supplying operating sectors, what is Resource Sector responsible for at the end of the incident?
cards.a: Checking the immediate area for equipment left at the scene.
cards.why: M.P. 202.07: Resource Sector is "also responsible for having the immediate area checked for equipment which may have been left at the scene upon termination."
opts: Checking the area for equipment left behind
Restocking every apparatus from the supply truck
Returning spare air bottles to Resource Management

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.09, what are the two principal reasons you ventilate a building?
cards.a: To prevent mushrooming and to gain (and maintain) entry.
cards.why: M.P. 202.09: "You ventilate a building principally for two reasons: To prevent mushrooming; To gain (and maintain) entry."
opts: Prevent mushrooming; gain and maintain entry
Cool the fire; improve visibility for search crews
Relieve heat on the roof; protect exposures
Reduce smoke damage; locate the seat of the fire

cards.q: You arrive at a bowstring-truss building with fire in the attic/truss space. Per M.P. 202.09, what is the policy?
cards.a: If safe to do so, quickly search the building and implement a defensive strategy.
cards.why: M.P. 202.09: "When fire is in the attic/truss space, and it is safe to do so, quickly search the building and implement a defensive strategy."
opts: Quickly search if safe, then go defensive
Make a quick, aggressive offensive attack from below
Send a ladder crew to vertically vent over the trusses
Go offensive, but limit interior crews to one air bottle

cards.q: Bowstring-roof building: fire is in one room and contents, with no evidence of extension into the truss space. Per M.P. 202.09, which strategy?
cards.a: A quick, aggressive, offensive strategy.
cards.why: M.P. 202.09: "When fire involves a room and contents with no evidence of extension to the attic/truss space—implement a quick, aggressive, offensive strategy."
opts: Quick search, then a defensive strategy
Defensive from the start, with no interior search
Vertical ventilation before any interior entry

cards.q: Attic fire in a single-family home with a tile roof. Per M.P. 202.09, can firefighters go to the roof?
cards.a: No. Firefighters are prohibited from going to the roof.
cards.why: M.P. 202.09: For interior and/or attic fires in single family residences with tiled roofs "fire fighters are prohibited from going to the roof."
opts: No, firefighters are prohibited from the roof
Yes, after careful evaluation of the roof profile
Yes, but only working from an aerial platform
Only while the fire is confined to a single room

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.09, which operating position is best for deciding whether a building needs ventilation, and where and when?
cards.a: The interior sector.
cards.why: M.P. 202.09: "The best operating position to determine if a building requires ventilation and the location and timing of that ventilation is the interior sector."

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.09, when should crews operate hoselines on the roof?
cards.a: Only to protect personnel and external exposures, unless Command orders a coordinated roof attack.
cards.why: M.P. 202.09: Do not operate lines down vent holes; "Operate roof lines only for the purpose of protecting personnel and external exposures unless Command orders a coordinated roof attack."
opts: To protect personnel and exposures, unless a roof attack is ordered
Down the vent hole once it's cut, to knock down the attic fire
Whenever fire and smoke start venting out of the roof holes
With a ladder pipe aimed through the ventilation opening

cards.q: Fire is progressing and you must attack from the unburned side through a locked door. Per M.P. 202.09, what do you do?
cards.a: Don't waste time picking locks; bash the door.
cards.why: M.P. 202.09: "The more critical the fire, the less important forcible entry damage becomes... don't waste time trying to pick the locks--bash the doors."
opts: Force the door; don't waste time on the lock
Pick the lock to limit damage, since loss control matters
Wait for the ladder company to do through-the-lock entry
Find an unlocked opening, even one on the fire side

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.10, a standard Attack Team consists of what?
cards.a: Two engine companies plus a ladder company.
cards.why: M.P. 202.10: "A standard Attack Team consists of two engine companies plus a ladder company," giving adequate water supply and support capability.
opts: One engine, one ladder and a rescue
Three engines and a battalion chief

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.10, what is a common deployment for an Attack Team?
cards.a: A forward pumper supplied by one or two lines from a key pumper on a hydrant.
cards.why: M.P. 202.10: "A common deployment for an Attack Team involves a 'forward' pumper supplied by one or two lines from a 'key' pumper on a hydrant."
opts: Forward pumper fed by a key pumper on a hydrant
Both engines on separate hydrants, each with its own line
The ladder pumping while both engines stretch handlines
Two forward pumpers fed by a tender shuttle from the key

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.10, once Command assigns an Attack Team, where does it fit in the organization?
cards.a: It reports to an existing Sector Officer or becomes an additional Sector.
cards.why: M.P. 202.10: "The Attack Team will either report to an existing Sector Officer or will become an additional Sector," and Command designates which officer assumes Sector responsibilities.
opts: Under an existing Sector, or as a new Sector
Always directly under Command as a separate team
In Staging until a Division is formed for it
Only under the Operations Section Chief

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12, what benchmark marks completion of the property conservation tactical priority?
cards.a: Loss stopped.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12: Search & Rescue = All clear; Fire Control = Fire under control; "Property Conservation = Loss stopped."

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12, which fire attack approach best supports loss control?
cards.a: Fighting the fire from the unburned portion of the building.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12: "Fighting the fire from the unburned portion will effect loss control"; attacks from the burning portion usually push heat and smoke through the building.
opts: Attacking from the burning portion to push fire out
A defensive attack to keep crews out of the building
Flooding the attic first to stop all extension

cards.q: After knockdown, water is pooling in the attic on top of the ceiling drywall. Per M.P. 202.12, what should you do?
cards.a: Use a drill or screwdriver to punch a small drainage hole so the water can escape.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12: Use "a drill or a screwdriver as a hole punch to allow the water to escape"; the small hole may save the ceiling and is easily patched.
opts: Punch a small drain hole with a drill or screwdriver
Pull the ceiling down from the corners to drain it
Leave it; the drywall will dry once the fire is out
Squeegee it in the attic toward an exterior wall

cards.q: You're checking the attic for extension. Per M.P. 202.12, what size inspection hole should you preferably cut?
cards.a: About 6" x 6" (and not at the corners).
cards.why: M.P. 202.12: "Cut small inspection holes, preferably 6\" x 6,\" to check attics," and don't pull drywall from corners, which can require replacing both walls and ceiling.

cards.q: Furniture is sitting in standing water and you have no blocks. Per M.P. 202.12, what can you use to raise it?
cards.a: Canned goods from the home.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12: Place blocks under furniture legs; "If no blocks are available, canned goods from the home serve the same purpose."
opts: Folded salvage covers under each leg
Rolled hall runners under the furniture
Nothing; carry it out onto the lawn

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12, why should you turn off the building's ventilation/AC system when appropriate?
cards.a: It spreads smoke to the rest of the structure and may contaminate the air handling system.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12: "The AC system will expose the remainder of the structure and might contaminate the air handling system (which could require its replacement)."
opts: It spreads smoke and can contaminate the air handler
It feeds oxygen to the fire and speeds flashover
It interferes with PPV fans set at the doorway
It creates a shock hazard for crews pulling ceiling

cards.q: While packaging a home after the fire, you find wet photo albums in a closet. Per M.P. 202.12, what do you do?
cards.a: Don't bag or box them wet; they need time to dry before packaging.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12: Keepsakes should be wrapped and boxed with contents marked, but "Do not bag or box wet items. They will need time to dry before packaging."
opts: Leave them unboxed so they can dry first
Seal them in plastic bags to stop more damage
Box them and mark the contents on the outside
Carry them out to the covered debris pile

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12A, what are the two salvage objectives?
cards.a: To reasonably stop or reduce the sources of damage, and to reasonably protect or remove contents.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12A: Salvage objectives are "To reasonably stop or reduce the sources of damage" and "To reasonably protect or remove contents."
opts: Stop damage sources; protect or remove contents
Recover valuables; document losses for insurance
Remove all contents; secure the building from looting
Ventilate smoke; finish overhaul before investigators

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12A, where should salvage efforts begin?
cards.a: In the areas most severely threatened, usually directly adjacent to or below the fire.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12A: Salvage should begin "in areas most severely threatened by damage. In most cases that will be areas directly adjacent to or below the fire area."
opts: Areas most threatened, usually beside or below the fire
The room of origin, then working outward from it
Floors above the fire, where smoke collects first
The rooms with the most expensive contents

cards.q: Contents can't practically be removed from a room near the fire. Per M.P. 202.12A, what should crews do?
cards.a: Group the contents in the center of the room, raise them off the floor and cover them.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12A: "When removal is not practical, contents should be grouped in the center of rooms, raised off of the floor and covered."
opts: Group in the center, raise off the floor, cover
Push against the walls and cover with plastic
Leave them where they sit and cover them in place
Stack them in a closet and close the door

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12A, what should be the primary considerations when deciding what to salvage?
cards.a: Replacement price and value (worth to the owner).
cards.why: M.P. 202.12A: "Replacement price and value should be the primary considerations"; business records or family mementos may have high value even if their price is low.
opts: Size and weight of the items
Closeness to the room of origin

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12A, who should meet the property owner to identify salvage priorities?
cards.a: Command and/or the Sector Officer.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12A: "Command and/or the Sector Officer should meet with the property owner or responsible party when available to determine/identify the salvage priorities."
opts: Any firefighter on the salvage crew

topics.title: Vol II: Fireground Support, Loss Control & Overhaul (202) (Part 2)
topics.sub: Overhaul, occupant services, pets and animals, fire cause investigation and Field Incident Reports.
concepts: 202.12B: Overhaul: last company officer leaving owns extinguishment; post-incident inspection before last unit leaves; C99 for fire watch; no standard overhaul on defensive fires.
202.12C: Occupant Services at all working structure fires; reports to Command (or loss control officer); walk-through only after Investigations approves.
202.12F: Pet rescue = loss control priority; no IV fluids for animals; strays to Maricopa County Animal Control; dangerous animals = Animal Control plus PD.
202.13 / 202.13A: Investigate after control and immediate salvage, before overhaul; investigator holds jurisdiction until releasing it; FIR by first-in company officer within 24 hours.

cards.q: A building rekindles the day after a fire. Per M.P. 202.12B, is that automatically evidence the original fire returned to flaming combustion?
cards.a: No. A rekindle should not be considered per se evidence of a return to flaming combustion of the original fire.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12B: Even reasonable overhaul may not eliminate all risk, and "A rekindle is not always and should not be considered per se evidence" of the original fire returning.
opts: No, it isn't per se evidence of that
Yes, it always means overhaul was incomplete
Yes, unless a fire investigator rules otherwise
Only if it occurs within 24 hours

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12B, who is responsible for fire extinguishment, when possible, as units clear the scene?
cards.a: The company officer last leaving the scene.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12B: The IC ensures reasonable overhaul; "The company officer last leaving the scene is responsible for fire extinguishment, when possible."
opts: The last company officer to leave
The IC who declared fire control

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12B, when must a post-incident inspection of the fire building be done?
cards.a: Before the last fire department unit leaves the scene.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12B: "A post incident inspection will be performed prior to the last fire department unit leaving the scene"; the IC decides if more are needed.
opts: Before the last FD unit leaves the scene
Within 4 hours after the last unit leaves
The next morning, by the first-due engine
Only when cellulose insulation is present

cards.q: The IC believes a burned building warrants a fire watch. Per M.P. 202.12B, who should be dispatched?
cards.why: M.P. 202.12B: "If The IC believes the circumstances warrant a fire watch, C99 should be dispatched," and C99 explains Fire Code fire watch requirements and cost to the owner.
opts: A ladder company to stand by

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12B, when may the IC waive post-incident inspections?
cards.a: When a fire watch is in place.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12B: "The IC may waive post incident inspections if a fire watch is in place."
opts: When a fire watch is in place
When the owner signs a release
When no cellulose insulation was found
When the TIC shows no hot spots

cards.q: Structure fire with cellulose insulation in the attic. Per M.P. 202.12B, what should crews and the investigator advise the owner/occupant?
cards.a: That they should not occupy the structure.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12B: With cellulose insulation, crews should "Meet with the owner/occupant and the fire investigator to advise the owner/occupant that they should not occupy the structure."
opts: They may move back in once the meter is pulled
All of the insulation has now been removed
They must hire a fire watch for 24 hours

cards.q: The fire was declared a Defensive Fire. Per M.P. 202.12B, how is overhaul handled?
cards.a: No standard overhaul; crews keep applying water from exterior positions until all fire is out.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12B: Overhaul "will not be conducted on structures that have been declared Defensive Fires"; crews apply water to hot spots from exterior positions until fully extinguished.
opts: Exterior water only, until all fire is out
Standard overhaul after an engineer clears it
Interior overhaul once the main body is knocked down
Overhaul from the doorways using a TIC only

cards.q: During overhaul you find possible evidence that can't stay where it is. Per M.P. 202.12B, how should it be removed?
cards.a: Under the direction of a fire investigator.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12B: When possible evidence stays untouched in its original location; "Where circumstances prohibit this, evidence should be removed under the direction of a fire investigator."
opts: Bagged by the crew and handed to the IC
Photographed, then moved outside by the crew
Moved by police officers on scene

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12C, when shall the IC establish an Occupant Services Sector?
cards.a: At all working structure fires, as early in the incident as practical (and at other incidents as needed).
cards.why: M.P. 202.12C: Occupant Services "shall be established by the Incident Commander at all working structure fires, and as early in the incident as is practical."
opts: At all working structure fires, as early as practical
Only at second alarm or greater fires
When an occupant asks for assistance
After the fire is declared under control

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12C, which additional resources are acceptable to request for staffing Occupant Services?
cards.a: An additional engine, ladder or battalion chief (staff personnel at prolonged incidents).
cards.why: M.P. 202.12C: "An additional engine, ladder, or battalion chief is acceptable"; at prolonged incidents Command may assign staff personnel.
opts: An engine, ladder or battalion chief
A police officer already on scene

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12C, who does Occupant Services report to once a loss control Branch/Section is assigned?
cards.a: The loss control officer.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12C: Occupant Services "shall report to Command unless a loss control Branch/Section is assigned, at which time he/she shall report to the loss control officer."

cards.q: Occupant Services wants to walk the owner through the burned structure. Per M.P. 202.12C, whose approval is needed first?
cards.a: The Investigations Sector (and only where safe).
cards.why: M.P. 202.12C: "Where safe to do so, and after approval from Investigations Sector, coordinate a 'Walk-through' of the structure with the responsible party."

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12C, when does Occupant Services stop providing service and support?
cards.a: When the customer indicates our services are no longer needed (it may go beyond incident termination).
cards.why: M.P. 202.12C: Provide "on-going service and support until the customer indicates our services are no longer needed"; responsibilities may extend beyond termination.
opts: When the customer says it's no longer needed
When the last company leaves the scene
When the Red Cross arrives on scene

cards.q: A family lost their living quarters and clothing in a house fire. Per M.P. 202.12C, who can provide clothing, food, toiletries and temporary housing?
cards.a: The American Red Cross.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12C: For residential fires with loss of living quarters and clothing, "The American Red Cross can provide some clothing, food, toiletries, and arrange for temporary shelter/housing."

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.12F, rescuing pets during an incident should take the same priority as what?
cards.a: Any loss control activity.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12F: "Rescuing pets or animals during an incident should take the same priority as any loss control activity," weighing risk to crews against a positive outcome.

cards.q: You're treating an injured dog pulled from a house fire. Per M.P. 202.12F, which care is NOT allowed?
cards.a: Giving fluids intravenously.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12F: Animal injuries can be treated like human BLS injuries (pressure, cooling burns, oxygen, splints), but "At no time... should any attempt be made to provide fluids intravenously."

cards.q: On a medical call you find a stray, uninjured dog. Per M.P. 202.12F, who is the call referred to?
cards.a: Maricopa County Animal Control.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12F: "For stray, uninjured animals, the call should be referred to the Maricopa County Animal Control."

cards.q: An aggressive animal is a danger to people on scene. Per M.P. 202.12F, who responds?
cards.a: Animal Control, and PD should also be requested.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12F: "When there is a danger to human safety, Animal Control will respond. (Also request that PD respond.)"
opts: Animal Control, and request PD as well
The Humane Society, and request PD as well
The AZ SPCA, with an engine standing by
Arizona Livestock with the ranking officer

cards.q: A badly injured animal is taken to an emergency vet by the FD and the owner can't be identified. Per M.P. 202.12F, who pays?
cards.a: The ASPCA.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12F: Cost goes to the owner, "or if the owner cannot be identified, then ASPCA will pay"; no cost is incurred by the Department or the member.

cards.q: You transported a rider who fell from a horse. Per M.P. 202.12F, which is the proper agency for the horse?
cards.a: Arizona Livestock.
cards.why: M.P. 202.12F: In the horse example, "The proper agency in this case is Arizona Livestock," though ASPCA may help secure the animal meanwhile.

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.13, which of these fires requires a Fire Investigator to respond?
cards.a: A dumpster fire with an identified suspect in custody.
cards.why: M.P. 202.13: Investigators respond to "Vehicle, field, or dumpster fires that have an identified suspect in custody"; car fires from the engine area, no-suspect trash fires and known accidental fires do not need one.
opts: Dumpster fire with a suspect in custody
Car fire that started in the engine area
Grass fire with no suspect in custody
Stove fire with food remains on the stove

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.13, at what point in operations should the fire investigation be performed?
cards.a: After fire control and immediate salvage, but before removing contents and overhaul.
cards.why: M.P. 202.13: Investigation "should be performed after fire control activities, immediate salvage, but prior to removing contents and overhaul actions."
opts: After control and immediate salvage, before overhaul
After overhaul is done and the scene is secured
Before fire control, while burn patterns are visible
After the contents are removed and the floor is clear

cards.q: A Fire Investigator is responding to your fire. Per M.P. 202.13, what should companies on scene do?
cards.a: Delay non-essential overhaul and secure the fire scene until the investigator arrives.
cards.why: M.P. 202.13: Companies "shall delay non-essential overhaul and secure the fire scene until the investigator arrives"; activities that may alter the scene stop until authorized.
opts: Hold non-essential overhaul and secure the scene
Finish overhaul so the investigator has a clean scene
Return to quarters and leave the scene unattended
Start removing contents to a safe outside location

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.13, once Command turns jurisdiction of the fire area over to the Investigator, when does it return to Command?
cards.a: When the Investigator releases it back to Command.
cards.why: M.P. 202.13: "The Fire Investigator retains jurisdiction until the Investigator releases it back to Command."
opts: When the IC terminates the incident

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.13, when should crews try to identify the responsible party and witnesses at a fire scene?
cards.a: As soon as possible; it shall not be delayed until the investigator is on scene.
cards.why: M.P. 202.13: Identifying the RP and witnesses "must be made as soon as possible and shall not be delayed until the investigator is on the scene."
opts: As soon as possible, without waiting
Only when no police are on scene
After overhaul, once the scene is quiet

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.13, which fireground activity presents the greatest potential for damage to evidence?
cards.a: Overhaul.
cards.why: M.P. 202.13: "Overhaul presents the greatest potential for damage to evidence" used by investigators and police in later prosecution.

cards.q: Fire fatality at a structure fire. Per M.P. 202.13, who is responsible for the death investigation?
cards.a: The Phoenix Police Department.
cards.why: M.P. 202.13: In joint investigations, Fire Investigators determine origin and cause, while "Phoenix Police are responsible for conducting the death investigation."

cards.q: A homeowner asks for information about the fire for an insurance claim; no investigator was needed. Per M.P. 202.13, what can the company officer give them?
cards.a: The fire department incident number.
cards.why: M.P. 202.13: "the company officer can give the fire department incident number, which will enable the victim to access fire department information regarding the fire."
opts: A printed copy of the F.I.R.
A signed statement of the cause

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.13A, how soon after an incident must a Field Incident Report (FIR) be entered?
cards.a: Within 24 hours.
cards.why: M.P. 202.13A: "FIRs must be entered within 24 hours of the incident."

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.13A, who completes the FIR for a fire response?
cards.a: The company officer of the first responding unit, unless a Fire Investigator responds.
cards.why: M.P. 202.13A: "The company officer of the first responding unit is responsible for completing the FIR unless a Fire Investigator responds to investigate."
opts: First-in company officer, unless an investigator responds
The IC, whether or not an investigator responds
The responding Fire Investigator, on every fire
The Battalion Chief who had command

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.13A, who may audit FIRs for quality assurance?
cards.a: Supervisors at the Battalion Chief level or higher.
cards.why: M.P. 202.13A: "Supervisors at the Battalion Chief level or higher may audit FIRs for quality assurance."

cards.q: Per M.P. 202.13A, what role does the FIR play when a fire's origin and cause are clear and no investigator is needed?
cards.a: It serves as the official initial investigation record.
cards.why: M.P. 202.13A: For clear origin and cause, "the company officer's FIR will serve as the official initial investigation record." FIRs are legal documents.
opts: An internal note not used as a legal record
A draft the investigator must rewrite
A statistics form only, not about cause

topics.title: Vol II: EMS Sectors & Multi-Casualty (203)
topics.sub: Multi-patient and mass casualty operations: EMS responsibilities, triage, extrication, treatment, transportation, medical supply and the Medical Safety Officer.
concepts: 203.01: Multi-patient procedures start at 2-1-Medical; MCI = 25-100 patients, disaster = 100+; EMS benchmarks: Triage Report and "All IMMEDIATES Transported."
203.01: Triage tags at 3+ IMMEDIATES or 10+ patients; Level II Staging on all 1st Alarm Medical+; red/yellow/green salvage covers mark treatment areas.
203.02: RAMP = Rapid Assessment of Mental Status and Pulse; declare RAMP by radio; report Immediate, Delayed, Dead/Dying, INA; triage tape on right arm.
203.03: Extrication: 1 company per 5 victims; ladders for forcible extrication; heavy equipment through Command; face-to-face comms with messengers.
203.04: Treatment: 1 company per 4 patients; 1 salvage cover = 3 patients; fill from exit toward entrance; extended treatment only if no transport available.
203.05 / 203.05A: Transportation: hospital status via Dispatch on Med-9; rescues to loading area no more than 2 at a time; leap-frog MINORs; pull tracking slips; Branch gets its own channel.
203.06 / 203.06A: Medical Supply Sector on 3-Alarm Medical+ (MS19 + EMS supply truck), reports to Command under 20 patients; MSO is a licensed practitioner in Safety Section/Rehab.

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.01, a "mass casualty incident" involves how many patients?
cards.a: 25 to 100 patients.
cards.why: M.P. 203.01: "A 'mass casualty incident' is defined as any incident involving 25 to 100 patients"; more than 100 is a "disaster."

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.01, the first-arriving company officer implements multi-patient/MCI procedures on EMS incidents requiring what commitment?
cards.a: A two-and-one medical (2-1-M) or greater.
cards.why: M.P. 203.01: It is the first-arriving company officer's responsibility to implement these procedures "on EMS incidents requiring the commitment of a two-and-one medical (2-1-M) or greater."
opts: Any call with two or more patients

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.01, triage tags should be used any time there are how many patients?
cards.a: Three or more IMMEDIATE patients, or more than ten patients.
cards.why: M.P. 203.01: "Triage tags should be used any time there are three (3) or more IMMEDIATE patients or more than ten (10) patients."
opts: Any 2nd Alarm Medical, regardless of count

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.01, after IMMEDIATE patients, which group is next in the treat-and-transport priority order?
cards.a: DELAYED patients upgraded to IMMEDIATE.
cards.why: M.P. 203.01: Priority order is "1. IMMEDIATE 2. DELAYED patients upgraded to IMMEDIATE 3. DELAYED 4. MINOR."

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.01, what are the two EMS tactical objectives to complete on any multi-patient/MCI incident?
cards.a: Completion of a Triage Report and the declaration of "All IMMEDIATES Transported."
cards.why: M.P. 203.01: The EMS tactical objectives are "Completion of a 'Triage Report'" and "Declaration of 'All IMMEDIATES Transported'."
opts: Treatment Area Set Up; Triage Complete

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.01, which medical incidents require a Level II Staging area for all FD resources, including rescues?
cards.a: All First Alarm Medical incidents or greater.
cards.why: M.P. 203.01: "All First-Alarm-Medical Incidents (or greater) require a Level II Staging Area for all fire department resources, including rescue companies."

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.01, colored salvage covers mark the treatment areas. Which color designates DELAYED patients?
cards.a: Yellow.
cards.why: M.P. 203.01: Colored salvage covers "(red, yellow and green)" designate treatment areas for IMMEDIATE, DELAYED or MINOR patients, respectively.

cards.q: A building collapse has victims in a hazardous area. Per M.P. 203.01, where is triage usually performed in this case?
cards.a: At the entrance to the treatment area, after victims are removed to a safe area.
cards.why: M.P. 203.01: With building collapse or hazmat release it may be better to remove victims to a safe area; "In these cases, triage will be performed at the entrance to the treatment area."
opts: In place, where each victim is found
At the Level II Staging area

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.01, at an initial multi-patient response, how long does the first company's triage function normally last?
cards.a: 4 to 6 minutes.
cards.why: M.P. 203.01: "The triage function should be performed by the first arriving company. Normally, it will last 4-6 minutes."

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.02, what does RAMP triage stand for?
cards.a: Rapid Assessment of Mental Status and Pulse.
cards.why: M.P. 203.02: RAMP is "Rapid Assessment of Mental Status and Pulse" triage, and can be used on any incident to make it a conditioned response.
opts: Rapid Assessment of Mental Status and Pulse
Rapid Assessment of Mobility and Perfusion

cards.q: Command or Triage decides RAMP triage is needed because patients exceed resources. Per M.P. 203.02, what must happen?
cards.a: Declare it on the radio to AHQ or Command so all responding and on-scene units know RAMP is in use.
cards.why: M.P. 203.02: "a declaration on the radio to AHQ or Command should be transmitted so that all responding, and on-scene units know RAMP is being utilized."
opts: Declare RAMP on the radio to AHQ or Command
Notify receiving hospitals through Med-9 first
Assign a Medical Branch Director before starting
Have Transportation begin pulling tracking slips

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.02, a Triage Report includes the number of patients in which categories?
cards.a: Immediate, Delayed, Dead/Dying and Involved Needs Assessment (INA).
cards.why: M.P. 203.02: "A Triage Report should include the number of Immediate, Delayed, Dead/Dying, and Involved Needs Assessment (INA) patients."

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.02, where is triage tape placed on a patient?
cards.a: On the right arm.
cards.why: M.P. 203.02: Patients are "accounted for with triage tape appropriately (right arm)."

cards.q: Under RAMP, a Dead/Dying patient still isn't breathing after lifesaving interventions. Per M.P. 203.02, what do you do?
cards.a: Consider the patient dead; they can be left in place.
cards.why: M.P. 203.02: Dead/Dying patients are reassessed as resources allow; "If not breathing after lifesaving interventions, they are considered dead and can be left in place."
opts: Consider them dead and leave them in place
Move them first so they can be re-triaged
Upgrade them to Immediate and transport
Tag them Delayed and recheck in 10 minutes

cards.q: There's an immediate threat to patients and responders where victims lie. Per M.P. 203.02, how is triage handled?
cards.a: Move the patients to a safe area, then triage them.
cards.why: M.P. 203.02: "If there is an immediate threat to the patients or responders, triage can be performed after the patients are moved to a safe area."
opts: Move them to safety, then triage
Triage everyone in place before moving anyone
Hold off on triage until the hazard is mitigated
Triage only the patients able to walk out

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.03, what is a reasonable initial commitment of companies to the Extrication Sector?
cards.a: One company per five victims.
cards.why: M.P. 203.03: "A reasonable guideline is an initial commitment of one company per five (5) victims."

cards.q: In a bus crash, DELAYED patients are blocking access to an IMMEDIATE patient. Per M.P. 203.03, what may happen?
cards.a: The DELAYED patients may be removed to treatment ahead of the IMMEDIATE patient.
cards.why: M.P. 203.03: "In some cases of confined entrapment, removing 'DELAYED' patients may occur before access can be gained to 'IMMEDIATE' patients."
opts: Leave them; IMMEDIATES must always go first
Re-tag the DELAYED patients as IMMEDIATE
Stop and wait for a heavy rescue company

cards.q: Victims at an MCI require forcible extrication. Per M.P. 203.03, which companies should be assigned?
cards.a: Ladder companies.
cards.why: M.P. 203.03: "When victims require forcible extrication, ladder companies should be assigned," and ladder apparatus is brought in close to the scene.

cards.q: Extrication needs wreckers, cranes or cutting torches. Per M.P. 203.03, how are they obtained?
cards.a: They must be requested through Command.
cards.why: M.P. 203.03: "If the extrication requires specialized equipment (i.e., wreckers, cranes, cutting torches), these must be requested through Command."

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.03, how should communications within the Extrication Sector be handled?
cards.a: Face-to-face, with company officers using messengers to relay information to the sector officer.
cards.why: M.P. 203.03: "Face-to-face communications should be used within the sector. Company officers should use messengers to relay information to the sector officer."
opts: Face-to-face, with messengers to the sector officer
Over Med-9 through the Dispatch Center
Through Command on the main fireground channel

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.03, where should most ALS personnel at an MCI be assigned?
cards.a: To the Treatment Sector (with some paramedics in Extrication for extended extrications).
cards.why: M.P. 203.03: "Most ALS personnel should be assigned to the Treatment Sector," though some may go to Extrication for critical patients in extended extrication.

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.04, during major incidents what is the initial staffing objective for the Treatment Sector?
cards.a: One company per four patients (one rescuer per patient).
cards.why: M.P. 203.04: Treatment typically needs the heaviest commitment; "one company per four (4) patients should be the initial objective (one rescuer per patient)."

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.04, one salvage cover provides working room for up to how many patients?
cards.a: Three patients.
cards.why: M.P. 203.04: "One salvage cover provides ample working room for up to three patients."

cards.q: You're setting up a treatment area. Per M.P. 203.04, where are the first-arriving patients placed?
cards.a: Near the exit point, filling from the exit toward the entrance.
cards.why: M.P. 203.04: "First arriving patients should be placed near the exit point. Rescuers should first fill from exit towards the entrance" so no one steps over patients.
opts: Near the exit, filling toward the entrance
Near the entrance, filling toward the exit
In the center, filling outward to the edges
Along one side, in order of arrival

cards.q: A patient who was never triaged walks up to the treatment area. Per M.P. 203.04, what happens?
cards.a: They are triaged and tagged at the entrance, and the Treatment officer sends Command a Triage Update.
cards.why: M.P. 203.04: "Non-triaged patients arriving at the treatment area must be triaged and tagged at the entrance," and the Treatment officer forwards a "Triage Update" to Command.
opts: Triage and tag at the entrance; send a Triage Update
Send them back out to the Triage Sector officer to be tagged
Place them in DELAYED until a paramedic can reassess them
Direct them to the MINOR Assembly Area without tagging

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.04, where will ALS treatment primarily be given?
cards.a: In the IMMEDIATE treatment area.
cards.why: M.P. 203.04: "ALS treatment will be given primarily in the 'IMMEDIATE' treatment area," with mostly BLS personnel in the DELAYED area.

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.04, when should extended on-scene treatment be considered?
cards.a: Only when immediate transportation is not available.
cards.why: M.P. 203.04: "The only time extended treatment should be considered is when immediate transportation is not available"; otherwise transport takes priority.
opts: Only when transport isn't immediately available
For every IMMEDIATE patient before loading
When the receiving hospital requests stabilization
Whenever enough ALS personnel are on scene

cards.q: Patients will be treated in place. Per M.P. 203.04, what's the goal resource assignment for each patient?
cards.a: One ALS or BLS company and one Rescue per patient, resources permitting.
cards.why: M.P. 203.04: For treatment in place, "The goal will be to assign one ALS or BLS company and one Rescue to each patient, resources permitting."
opts: One ALS or BLS company and one Rescue
One ALS company and two Rescues
One Rescue with no company assigned

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.05, rescues are brought from off-site staging into the patient loading area how many at a time?
cards.a: No more than two at a time.
cards.why: M.P. 203.05: "Rescues should be staged off site and brought in to the loading area as needed, no more than two at a time."

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.05, how does the Transportation Sector determine hospital availability?
cards.a: By contacting Dispatch on Med-9.
cards.why: M.P. 203.05: Transportation will "Determine hospital availability status by contacting Dispatch on Med-9."

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.05, where is it generally preferred to send MINOR patients?
cards.a: "Leap-frog" them to distant hospitals so DELAYED patients get shorter trips to closer facilities.
cards.why: M.P. 203.05: "it is preferred to 'leap-frog' MINOR patients to distant hospitals to minimize transport times for DELAYED patients to closer facilities."
opts: To distant hospitals, keeping closer ones for DELAYED
To the closest hospitals, since they load fastest
To urgent care centers only, never to hospitals
To the same hospital as the IMMEDIATE patients

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.05, how should helicopters be used at a multi-patient incident?
cards.a: To take critical patients to more distant facilities, letting closer hospitals take ground patients.
cards.why: M.P. 203.05: "Helicopters should be used to transport critical patients to more distance medical facilities, allowing closer hospitals to receive patients by ground ambulance."
opts: Critical patients to more distant facilities
MINOR patients, to free up ground rescues
Any patient bound for a Level I trauma center
Only patients ground units cannot reach

cards.q: A patient is about to be loaded into a rescue. Per M.P. 203.05, what does the Transportation Sector Officer do with the triage tag?
cards.a: Remove the transportation tracking slip and write the transport unit and hospital on it.
cards.why: M.P. 203.05: The officer "will remove a transportation tracking slip from each triage tag and write in the transport unit and hospital destination," keeping the slips for accountability.
opts: Pull the tracking slip; write unit and hospital on it
Remove the whole tag and hand it to Command
Leave it on and radio the tag number to Dispatch
Give the tracking slip to the transporting crew

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.05, how should ALS crews transporting from an MCI handle medical direction?
cards.a: Operate under Standing Orders and not patch for Medical Direction unless necessary.
cards.why: M.P. 203.05: "ALS personnel should operate under Standing Orders and not patch for Medical Direction unless necessary."
opts: Standing Orders; patch only if necessary
Patch for Medical Direction on every IMMEDIATE
Patch to the hospital before leaving the scene

cards.q: Helicopters will be used at a multi-patient incident. Per M.P. 203.05, what is the minimum assignment to the landing zone?
cards.a: At least one Engine Company, with an LZ Sector designated.
cards.why: M.P. 203.05: Transportation should establish an LZ a safe distance from the scene, "assign at least one Engine Company to the LZ and designate an 'LZ Sector.'"

cards.q: With multiple treatment areas, per M.P. 203.05A where is the Transportation Branch Director stationed?
cards.a: At a central location, preferably at or close to the Command Post.
cards.why: M.P. 203.05A: "The Transportation Branch Director will be stationed at a central location, preferably at or close to the Command Post."
opts: Centrally, at or near the Command Post
At the Level II Staging area

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.05A, each sector under the Transportation Branch (East/West Transportation, Staging, LZ) requires at least what?
cards.a: At least one full company.
cards.why: M.P. 203.05A: Each Sector (e.g., "East Transportation Sector," "Staging," "LZ") "will require at least one full company."

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.05A, what radio arrangement should the Transportation Branch use?
cards.a: A separate radio channel assigned exclusively to the Transportation Branch.
cards.why: M.P. 203.05A: "a separate radio channel should be assigned exclusively to the Transportation Branch"; the Branch Director handles all communications with Dispatch.

cards.q: At a multi-site MCI, a rescue at East Transportation is ready to load. Per M.P. 203.05A, who decides the destination hospital?
cards.a: The Transportation Branch Director.
cards.why: M.P. 203.05A: The Sector officer reports patients and severity to the Branch, and "The Branch Director will then advise the Transportation Sector officer of the destination hospital."

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.06, a Medical Supply Sector shall be established on which incidents?
cards.a: All 3-Alarm Medical (or greater) incidents, using at least one fire company.
cards.why: M.P. 203.06: "a Medical Supply Sector shall be established during all 3-Alarm Medical (or greater) major medical incidents using a minimum of one fire company."

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.06, which units does Dispatch special call for the Medical Supply Sector?
cards.a: Medical Support 19 from the airport and an EMS supply truck from Resource Management.
cards.why: M.P. 203.06: "Dispatch will special call Medical Support 19 from the airport and an EMS supply truck from Resource Management to the scene."
opts: MS19 from the airport and an EMS supply truck
Two Rescues and a Battalion Chief
A ladder company and the Rehab unit
A Hazmat unit and an EMS supply truck

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.06, at an incident with fewer than 20 patients, who does the Medical Supply Sector report to?
cards.a: Command.
cards.why: M.P. 203.06: "At incidents with less than 20 patients, Medical Supply Sector will report to Command"; at larger MCIs it reports to Medical Branch or Logistics.

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.06A, which section is the Medical Safety Officer assigned to, and in which sector does the MSO work?
cards.a: The Safety Section, working in the Rehab Sector.
cards.why: M.P. 203.06A: "The MSO would be tasked through the Safety Section and work in the Rehab Sector," partnered with a Command Officer.

cards.q: Per M.P. 203.06A, who fills the Medical Safety Officer position?
cards.a: A physician/licensed medical practitioner.
cards.why: M.P. 203.06A: The MSO places "a licensed medical practitioner as part of the strategic level"; requirements list physician/licensed medical professional with firefighter occupational medicine.

cards.q: At a multiple-casualty WMD incident, per M.P. 203.06A the MSO may function as what, assigned to Operations?
cards.a: Medical Triage Officer.
cards.why: M.P. 203.06A: If needed, the MSO would act as a medical triage officer at multiple-casualty WMD incidents, "assigned to the Operations Section."

notes: M.P. 202.12D (Positive Pressure Ventilation) has no usable text: the file only says "This SOP is currently out for review." No cards written.
M.P. 203.01 (03/00-R) defines a multi-patient incident as "fewer than twenty (25) patients" (word and numeral conflict). No card tests that number; MCI (25-100) and disaster (100+) are tested.

M.P. 203.01, 203.03 and 203.04 (all 03/00) use IMMEDIATE/DELAYED/MINOR categories, S.T.A.R.T./Central Arizona triage and triage tags, while M.P. 203.02 (05/26-R) uses RAMP with Immediate/Delayed/Dead-Dying/INA categories and triage tape. The older MPs look outdated relative to 203.02; cards cite each MP as written.
M.P. 203.02 page 3 is titled "RAMP Triage" but has no extractable text (probably a flowchart image), so the RAMP algorithm itself isn't carded.
M.P. 203.01 says the Triage Report is radioed "to Alarm" in one place and to Command elsewhere; 203.02 says to Command.
M.P. 203.06A (10/04-N) is written as a proposal ("would respond", "would be assigned"); cards treat its stated assignments as policy.
M.P. 202.12 and 202.12B both cover securing the scene (plastic over vent holes/windows, remove glass shards); carded only once each on other points to avoid duplicates.
